speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न विश्वासाज्जातु परस्य गेहं
गच्छेन्नरश्चेतयानो विकाले ।
न चत्वरे निशि तिष्ठेन्निगूढो
न राजन्यां योषितं प्रार्थयीत ॥
iast:
na viśvāsājjātu parasya gehaṃ
gacchennaraścetayāno vikāle |
na catvare niśi tiṣṭhennigūḍho
na rājanyāṃ yoṣitaṃ prārthayīta ||
english: A careful person should never go to another's house at an odd hour out of trust, nor stand hidden at a crossroads at night, nor court a woman of the royal household.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न निह्नवं सत्र गतस्य गच्छेत्
संसृष्ट मन्त्रस्य कुसङ्गतस्य ।
न च ब्रूयान्नाश्वसामि त्वयीति
स कारणं व्यपदेशं तु कुर्यात् ॥
iast:
na nihnavaṃ satra gatasya gacchet
saṃsṛṣṭa mantrasya kusaṅgatasya |
na ca brūyānnāśvasāmi tvayīti
sa kāraṇaṃ vyapadeśaṃ tu kuryāt ||
english: One should not contradict a man sitting in an assembly whose counsel is mixed with bad company; nor should one say 'I do not trust you', but should give a reason or excuse.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
घृणी राजा पुंश्चली राजभृत्यः
पुत्रो भ्राता विधवा बाल पुत्रा ।
सेना जीवी चोद्धृत भक्त एव
व्यवहारे वै वर्जनीयाः स्युरेते ॥
iast:
ghṛṇī rājā puṃścalī rājabhṛtyaḥ
putro bhrātā vidhavā bāla putrā |
senā jīvī coddhṛta bhakta eva
vyavahāre vai varjanīyāḥ syurete ||
english: A compassionate king, a loose woman, a king's servant, a son, a brother, a widow with a young son, one who lives by soldiering, and one who has lost his position: these should be avoided in transactions.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
गुणा दश स्नानशीलं भजन्ते
बलं रूपं स्वरवर्णप्रशुद्धिः ।
स्पर्शश्च गन्धश्च विशुद्धता च
श्रीः सौकुमार्यं प्रवराश्च नार्यः ॥
iast:
guṇā daśa snānaśīlaṃ bhajante
balaṃ rūpaṃ svaravarṇapraśuddhiḥ |
sparśaśca gandhaśca viśuddhatā ca
śrīḥ saukumāryaṃ pravarāśca nāryaḥ ||
english: Ten benefits come to one who bathes regularly: strength, beauty, a clear voice and complexion, softness of touch, fragrance, purity, fortune, delicacy, and the finest women.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
गुणाश्च षण्मितभुक्तं भजन्ते
आरोग्यमायुश्च सुखं बलं च ।
अनाविलं चास्य भवेदपत्यं
न चैनमाद्यून इति क्षिपन्ति ॥
iast:
guṇāśca ṣaṇmitabhuktaṃ bhajante
ārogyamāyuśca sukhaṃ balaṃ ca |
anāvilaṃ cāsya bhavedapatyaṃ
na cainamādyūna iti kṣipanti ||
english: Six benefits come to one who eats moderately: health, long life, happiness and strength; his children are healthy, and no one mocks him as a glutton.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अकर्म शीलं च महाशनं च
लोकद्विष्टं बहु मायं नृशंसम् ।
अदेशकालज्ञमनिष्ट वेषम्
एतान्गृहे न प्रतिवासयीत ॥
iast:
akarma śīlaṃ ca mahāśanaṃ ca
lokadviṣṭaṃ bahu māyaṃ nṛśaṃsam |
adeśakālajñamaniṣṭa veṣam
etāngṛhe na prativāsayīta ||
english: One who is idle, a glutton, hated by people, very deceitful, cruel, ignorant of place and time, and improperly dressed: one should not let these live in one's house.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
कदर्यमाक्रोशकमश्रुतं च
वराक सम्भूतममान्य मानिनम् ।
निष्ठूरिणं कृतवैरं कृतघ्नम्
एतान्भृतार्तोऽपि न जातु याचेत् ॥
iast:
kadaryamākrośakamaśrutaṃ ca
varāka sambhūtamamānya māninam |
niṣṭhūriṇaṃ kṛtavairaṃ kṛtaghnam
etānbhṛtārto'pi na jātu yācet ||
english: A miser, an abuser, the unlearned, the base-born who honours the dishonourable, the harsh, one who has made enemies, and the ungrateful: one should never beg from these, even in distress.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सङ्क्लिष्टकर्माणमतिप्रवादं
नित्यानृतं चादृढ भक्तिकं च ।
विकृष्टरागं बहुमानिनं चाप्य्
एतान्न सेवेत नराधमान्षट् ॥
iast:
saṅkliṣṭakarmāṇamatipravādaṃ
nityānṛtaṃ cādṛḍha bhaktikaṃ ca |
vikṛṣṭarāgaṃ bahumāninaṃ cāpy
etānna seveta narādhamānṣaṭ ||
english: One of corrupt deeds, a slanderer, one always lying, one of unsteady devotion, one without affection, and one very conceited: one should not serve these six lowest of people.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सहायबन्धना ह्यर्थाः सहायाश्चार्थबन्धनाः ।
अन्योन्यबन्धनावेतौ विनान्योन्यं न सिध्यतः ॥
iast:
sahāyabandhanā hyarthāḥ sahāyāścārthabandhanāḥ |
anyonyabandhanāvetau vinānyonyaṃ na sidhyataḥ ||
english: Aims are bound to helpers, and helpers are bound to means; these two are bound to each other, and neither succeeds without the other.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
उत्पाद्य पुत्राननृणांश्च कृत्वा
वृत्तिं च तेभ्योऽनुविधाय कां चित् ।
स्थाने कुमारीः प्रतिपाद्य सर्वा
अरण्यसंस्थो मुनिवद्बुभूषेत् ॥
iast:
utpādya putrānanṛṇāṃśca kṛtvā
vṛttiṃ ca tebhyo'nuvidhāya kāṃ cit |
sthāne kumārīḥ pratipādya sarvā
araṇyasaṃstho munivadbubhūṣet ||
english: Having fathered sons and freed them from debt, having arranged some livelihood for them, and having given all daughters in marriage properly, one should wish to live in the forest as a sage.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
हितं यत्सर्वभूतानामात्मनश्च सुखावहम् ।
तत्कुर्यादीश्वरो ह्येतन्मूलं धर्मार्थसिद्धये ॥
iast:
hitaṃ yatsarvabhūtānāmātmanaśca sukhāvaham |
tatkuryādīśvaro hyetanmūlaṃ dharmārthasiddhaye ||
english: What is beneficial to all beings and brings happiness to oneself, the lord should do; this is the root of success in dharma and true benefit.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
बुद्धिः प्रभावस्तेजश्च सत्त्वमुत्थानमेव च ।
व्यवसायश्च यस्य स्यात्तस्यावृत्ति भयं कुतः ॥
iast:
buddhiḥ prabhāvastejaśca sattvamutthānameva ca |
vyavasāyaśca yasya syāttasyāvṛtti bhayaṃ kutaḥ ||
english: One who has intelligence, influence, energy, strength, enterprise and resolve: where is his fear of having no livelihood?

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
पश्य दोषान्पाण्डवैर्विग्रहे त्वं
यत्र व्यथेरन्नपि देवाः स शक्राः ।
पुत्रैर्वैरं नित्यमुद्विग्नवासो
यशः प्रणाशो द्विषतां च हर्षः ॥
iast:
paśya doṣānpāṇḍavairvigrahe tvaṃ
yatra vyatherannapi devāḥ sa śakrāḥ |
putrairvairaṃ nityamudvignavāso
yaśaḥ praṇāśo dviṣatāṃ ca harṣaḥ ||
english: See the evils in a conflict with the Pandavas, at which even the gods with Indra would tremble: enmity with your sons, living in constant anxiety, loss of fame and the joy of enemies.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
भीष्मस्य कोपस्तव चेन्द्र कल्प
द्रोणस्य राज्ञश्च युधिष्ठिरस्य ।
उत्सादयेल्लोकमिमं प्रवृद्धः
श्वेतो ग्रहस्तिर्यगिवापतन्खे ॥
iast:
bhīṣmasya kopastava cendra kalpa
droṇasya rājñaśca yudhiṣṭhirasya |
utsādayellokamimaṃ pravṛddhaḥ
śveto grahastiryagivāpatankhe ||
english: The anger of Bhishma, of you who are like Indra, of Drona and of King Yudhishthira, once roused, could destroy this world, like a white comet falling across the sky.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
तव पुत्रशतं चैव कर्णः पञ्च च पाण्डवाः ।
पृथिवीमनुशासेयुरखिलां सागराम्बराम् ॥
iast:
tava putraśataṃ caiva karṇaḥ pañca ca pāṇḍavāḥ |
pṛthivīmanuśāseyurakhilāṃ sāgarāmbarām ||
english: Your hundred sons, Karna and the five Pandavas could together rule the whole earth, clothed by the ocean.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
धार्तराष्ट्रा वनं राजन्व्याघ्राः पाण्डुसुता मताः ।
मा वनं छिन्धि स व्याघ्रं मा व्याघ्रान्नीनशो वनात् ॥
iast:
dhārtarāṣṭrā vanaṃ rājanvyāghrāḥ pāṇḍusutā matāḥ |
mā vanaṃ chindhi sa vyāghraṃ mā vyāghrānnīnaśo vanāt ||
english: Dhritarashtra's sons are a forest, king, and Pandu's sons are held to be the tigers. Do not cut down the forest with its tigers; do not drive the tigers out of the forest.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न स्याद्वनमृते व्याघ्रान्व्याघ्रा न स्युरृते वनम् ।
वनं हि रक्ष्यते व्याघ्रैर्व्याघ्रान्रक्षति काननम् ॥
iast:
na syādvanamṛte vyāghrānvyāghrā na syurṛte vanam |
vanaṃ hi rakṣyate vyāghrairvyāghrānrakṣati kānanam ||
english: There is no forest without tigers, and no tigers without a forest. The forest is protected by the tigers, and the tigers are protected by the forest.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न तथेच्छन्त्यकल्याणाः परेषां वेदितुं गुणान् ।
यथैषां ज्ञातुमिच्छन्ति नैर्गुण्यं पापचेतसः ॥
iast:
na tathecchantyakalyāṇāḥ pareṣāṃ vedituṃ guṇān |
yathaiṣāṃ jñātumicchanti nairguṇyaṃ pāpacetasaḥ ||
english: The ill-natured do not wish to learn others' virtues as much as the evil-minded wish to learn their faults.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अर्थसिद्धिं परामिच्छन्धर्ममेवादितश् चरेत् ।
न हि धर्मादपैत्यर्थः स्वर्गलोकादिवामृतम् ॥
iast:
arthasiddhiṃ parāmicchandharmamevāditaś caret |
na hi dharmādapaityarthaḥ svargalokādivāmṛtam ||
english: Wishing for the highest success in one's aims, one should practise dharma from the very beginning; for wealth does not depart from dharma, as nectar does not depart from heaven.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यस्यात्मा विरतः पापात्कल्याणे च निवेशितः ।
तेन सर्वमिदं बुद्धं प्रकृतिर्विकृतिर्श्च या ॥
iast:
yasyātmā virataḥ pāpātkalyāṇe ca niveśitaḥ |
tena sarvamidaṃ buddhaṃ prakṛtirvikṛtirśca yā ||
english: One whose self has turned away from wrong and is set on the good has understood all this, both nature and its changes.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यो धर्ममर्थं कामं च यथाकालं निषेवते ।
धर्मार्थकामसंयोगं योऽमुत्रेह च विन्दति ॥
iast:
yo dharmamarthaṃ kāmaṃ ca yathākālaṃ niṣevate |
dharmārthakāmasaṃyogaṃ yo'mutreha ca vindati ||
english: One who pursues dharma, wealth and pleasure each at its proper time gains the union of dharma, wealth and pleasure, both hereafter and here.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
संनियच्छति यो वेगमुत्थितं क्रोधहर्षयोः ।
स श्रियो भाजनं राजन्यश्चापत्सु न मुह्यति ॥
iast:
saṃniyacchati yo vegamutthitaṃ krodhaharṣayoḥ |
sa śriyo bhājanaṃ rājanyaścāpatsu na muhyati ||
english: One who restrains the rising force of anger and elation, and is not bewildered in misfortune, is a vessel of good fortune, king.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
बलं पञ्च विधं नित्यं पुरुषाणां निबोध मे ।
यत्तु बाहुबलं नाम कनिष्ठं बलमुच्यते ॥
iast:
balaṃ pañca vidhaṃ nityaṃ puruṣāṇāṃ nibodha me |
yattu bāhubalaṃ nāma kaniṣṭhaṃ balamucyate ||
english: Learn from me the five kinds of strength people always have. What is called strength of arm is said to be the lowest strength.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अमात्यलाभो भद्रं ते द्वितीयं बलमुच्यते ।
धनलाभस्तृतीयं तु बलमाहुर्जिगीषवः ॥
iast:
amātyalābho bhadraṃ te dvitīyaṃ balamucyate |
dhanalābhastṛtīyaṃ tu balamāhurjigīṣavaḥ ||
english: Gaining ministers, bless you, is called the second strength; gaining wealth, those who seek victory call the third strength.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यत्त्वस्य सहजं राजन्पितृपैतामहं बलम् ।
अभिजात बलं नाम तच्चतुर्थं बलं स्मृतम् ॥
iast:
yattvasya sahajaṃ rājanpitṛpaitāmahaṃ balam |
abhijāta balaṃ nāma taccaturthaṃ balaṃ smṛtam ||
english: The natural strength, king, that comes from father and grandfather, called strength of birth, is remembered as the fourth strength.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
येन त्वेतानि सर्वाणि सङ्गृहीतानि भारत ।
यद्बलानां बलं श्रेष्ठं तत्प्रज्ञा बलमुच्यते ॥
iast:
yena tvetāni sarvāṇi saṅgṛhītāni bhārata |
yadbalānāṃ balaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ tatprajñā balamucyate ||
english: But the strength by which all these are gathered together, Bharata, the best of all strengths, is called the strength of wisdom.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
महते योऽपकाराय नरस्य प्रभवेन्नरः ।
तेन वैरं समासज्य दूरस्थोऽस्मीति नाश्वसेत् ॥
iast:
mahate yo'pakārāya narasya prabhavennaraḥ |
tena vairaṃ samāsajya dūrastho'smīti nāśvaset ||
english: Having made an enemy of a person able to do one great harm, one should not feel secure thinking 'I am far away'.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
स्त्रीषु राजसु सर्पेषु स्वाध्याये शत्रुसेविषु ।
भोगे चायुषि विश्वासं कः प्राज्ञः कर्तुमर्हति ॥
iast:
strīṣu rājasu sarpeṣu svādhyāye śatruseviṣu |
bhoge cāyuṣi viśvāsaṃ kaḥ prājñaḥ kartumarhati ||
english: In women, kings and snakes, in one's own learning, in those who serve the enemy, in enjoyment and in life itself: what wise person would place trust?

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
प्रज्ञा शरेणाभिहतस्य जन्तोश्
चिकित्सकाः सन्ति न चौषधानि ।
न होममन्त्रा न च मङ्गलानि
नाथर्वणा नाप्यगदाः सुसिद्धाः ॥
iast:
prajñā śareṇābhihatasya jantoś
cikitsakāḥ santi na cauṣadhāni |
na homamantrā na ca maṅgalāni
nātharvaṇā nāpyagadāḥ susiddhāḥ ||
english: For a creature struck by the arrow of wisdom there are no physicians and no medicines, no sacrificial chants or blessings, no Atharvan spells nor well-made antidotes.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सर्पश्चाग्निश्च सिंहश्च कुलपुत्रश्च भारत ।
नावज्ञेया मनुष्येण सर्वे ते ह्यतितेजसः ॥
iast:
sarpaścāgniśca siṃhaśca kulaputraśca bhārata |
nāvajñeyā manuṣyeṇa sarve te hyatitejasaḥ ||
english: A snake, fire, a lion and a son of noble family, Bharata: none of these should be despised by a person, for all of them are full of power.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अग्निस्तेजो महल्लोके गूढस्तिष्ठति दारुषु ।
न चोपयुङ्क्ते तद्दारु यावन्नो दीप्यते परैः ॥
iast:
agnistejo mahalloke gūḍhastiṣṭhati dāruṣu |
na copayuṅkte taddāru yāvanno dīpyate paraiḥ ||
english: Fire, a great energy in the world, lies hidden in wood, and does not consume that wood until it is kindled by others.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
स एव खलु दारुभ्यो यदा निर्मथ्य दीप्यते ।
तदा तच्च वनं चान्यन्निर्दहत्याशु तेजसा ॥
iast:
sa eva khalu dārubhyo yadā nirmathya dīpyate |
tadā tacca vanaṃ cānyannirdahatyāśu tejasā ||
english: But when it is kindled from that wood by churning, it quickly burns that wood and the rest of the forest with its energy.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
एवमेव कुले जाताः पावकोपम तेजसः ।
क्षमावन्तो निराकाराः काष्ठेऽग्निरिव शेरते ॥
iast:
evameva kule jātāḥ pāvakopama tejasaḥ |
kṣamāvanto nirākārāḥ kāṣṭhe'gniriva śerate ||
english: So those born in noble families, with energy like fire, forbearing and showing no sign, lie quiet like fire in wood.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
लता धर्मा त्वं सपुत्रः शालाः पाण्डुसुता मताः ।
न लता वर्धते जातु महाद्रुममनाश्रिता ॥
iast:
latā dharmā tvaṃ saputraḥ śālāḥ pāṇḍusutā matāḥ |
na latā vardhate jātu mahādrumamanāśritā ||
english: You and your sons are a creeper, and Pandu's sons are held to be great sal trees. A creeper never grows without leaning on a great tree.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
वनं राजंस्त्वं सपुत्रोऽम्बिकेय
सिंहान्वने पाण्डवांस्तात विद्धि ।
सिंहैर्विहीनं हि वनं विनश्येत्
सिंहा विनश्येयुरृते वनेन ॥
iast:
vanaṃ rājaṃstvaṃ saputro'mbikeya
siṃhānvane pāṇḍavāṃstāta viddhi |
siṃhairvihīnaṃ hi vanaṃ vinaśyet
siṃhā vinaśyeyurṛte vanena ||
english: You and your sons, son of Ambika, are the forest; know the Pandavas, dear one, as the lions in it. A forest without lions perishes, and lions perish without a forest.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
ऊर्ध्वं प्राणा ह्युत्क्रामन्ति यूनः स्थविर आयति ।
प्रत्युत्थानाभिवादाभ्यां पुनस्तान्पतिपद्यते ॥
iast:
ūrdhvaṃ prāṇā hyutkrāmanti yūnaḥ sthavira āyati |
pratyutthānābhivādābhyāṃ punastānpatipadyate ||
english: The life-breaths of a young person rise up when an elder approaches; by rising and greeting him, he regains them.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
पीठं दत्त्वा साधवेऽभ्यागताय
आनीयापः परिनिर्णिज्य पादौ ।
सुखं पृष्ट्वा प्रतिवेद्यात्म संस्थं
ततो दद्यादन्नमवेक्ष्य धीरः ॥
iast:
pīṭhaṃ dattvā sādhave'bhyāgatāya
ānīyāpaḥ parinirṇijya pādau |
sukhaṃ pṛṣṭvā prativedyātma saṃsthaṃ
tato dadyādannamavekṣya dhīraḥ ||
english: Having given a seat to a good person who has come, bringing water and washing his feet, asking after his well-being and telling of one's own, the steady person should then give food, with care.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यस्योदकं मधुपर्कं च गां च
न मन्त्रवित्प्रतिगृह्णाति गेहे ।
लोभाद्भयादर्थकार्पण्यतो वा
तस्यानर्थं जीवितमाहुरार्याः ॥
iast:
yasyodakaṃ madhuparkaṃ ca gāṃ ca
na mantravitpratigṛhṇāti gehe |
lobhādbhayādarthakārpaṇyato vā
tasyānarthaṃ jīvitamāhurāryāḥ ||
english: When a learned guest will not accept water, honey-drink and a cow in someone's house because of the host's greed, fear or miserliness, the noble say that person's life is useless.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
चिकित्सकः शक्य कर्तावकीर्णी
स्तेनः क्रूरो मद्यपो भ्रूणहा च ।
सेनाजीवी श्रुतिविक्रायकश् च
भृशं प्रियोऽप्यतिथिर्नोदकार्हः ॥
iast:
cikitsakaḥ śakya kartāvakīrṇī
stenaḥ krūro madyapo bhrūṇahā ca |
senājīvī śrutivikrāyakaś ca
bhṛśaṃ priyo'pyatithirnodakārhaḥ ||
english: A physician, a surgeon, one who has broken his vow of celibacy, a thief, a cruel person, a drinker, one who kills embryos, one who lives by soldiering, and one who sells the Veda: however dear, such a guest is not worthy of water.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अविक्रेयं लवणं पक्वमन्नं दधि
क्षीरं मधु तैलं घृतं च ।
तिला मांसं मूलफलानि शाकं
रक्तं वासः सर्वगन्धा गुडश् च ॥
iast:
avikreyaṃ lavaṇaṃ pakvamannaṃ dadhi
kṣīraṃ madhu tailaṃ ghṛtaṃ ca |
tilā māṃsaṃ mūlaphalāni śākaṃ
raktaṃ vāsaḥ sarvagandhā guḍaś ca ||
english: Not to be sold are salt, cooked food, curd, milk, honey, oil and ghee, sesame, meat, roots and fruits, vegetables, red cloth, all perfumes and jaggery.
